title: Checkout errors after a payments deploy
goal: Restore checkout for customers as fast as possible without losing or corrupting payment records.

incident.summary: At 14:02 payments-service v2.31 was deployed. Since 14:04 checkout returns HTTP 500 for about 12% of requests and p99 latency on the payments API is 4.8 seconds (normal is 300 ms). The primary payments database is at 92% CPU.

options.name: Roll back to v2.30
options.description: Redeploy the previous payments-service build (v2.30) to all pods through the normal CI/CD pipeline.

options.name: Disable the smart-retries flag
options.description: Turn off the smart-retries feature flag in the flag service. The change applies to running pods within about one minute and can be turned back on instantly.

options.name: Fail over to a larger database
options.description: Promote a larger replica instance to be the new primary payments database. Requires a primary failover of roughly two minutes.

options.name: Fail over checkout to us-west-2
options.description: Shift all checkout traffic from us-east-1 to the standby us-west-2 region using DNS weights.

options.name: Ship a forward hotfix
options.description: Have the payments team write a code fix on top of v2.31 and ship it as v2.32 through CI/CD.

criteria.name: Error reduction
criteria.question: How much would carrying out the option reduce the checkout errors customers are seeing?
levels: Would not reduce the errors, or would make them worse
Small reduction; most customers would still see errors
Large reduction; a few customers would still see errors
Would very likely stop the errors

criteria.name: Time to effect
criteria.question: How quickly would the option take effect for customers once someone starts it?

criteria.name: Safety
criteria.question: How safe is carrying out the option right now, in terms of causing new or wider damage?
levels: High chance of a new or wider outage, or of damaging data
Very low risk and easy to undo

criteria.name: Evidence fit
criteria.question: How well does the evidence in the incident timeline support that the option addresses the actual cause?
levels: The evidence points to a different cause

constraints.name: No payment data loss
constraints.question: Would carrying out the option risk losing or corrupting committed customer payment records?

constraints.name: Respect incident commander orders
constraints.question: Has the incident commander explicitly forbidden this kind of action in the incident timeline?

updates.title: Deploy diff reviewed
updates.text: The v2.31 diff turns on the new smart-retries feature flag by default. Since 14:02, retry traffic from payments-service to the primary database has tripled.

updates.title: Database team report
updates.text: Replicas are 40 seconds behind the primary because of the write load. A primary failover right now would drop the most recent committed writes, including payment records.

updates.title: Standby region check
updates.text: The us-west-2 standby region reads and writes through the same primary payments database in us-east-1. It runs the same v2.31 build.

updates.title: Incident commander order
updates.text: Incident commander: no new code changes or new builds go to production until the error rate is under 1%. Configuration and flag changes are allowed.

updates.title: Rollback artifact problem
updates.text: The v2.30 build artifact expired from the registry. A rollback would need a fresh v2.30 build, which takes about 25 minutes in CI.
